content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm trying to upload a [document] program to the SD card of a [product_name] version 8. Everything worked fine earlier, but after I added some images from the default libraries, I started getting the error: Download Failed! SD Card isn't ready. I haven't made any major setting changes, just updated the webpage and tried to upload the new version. The only new items were those default library images. Does anyone know any fixes or troubleshooting steps for this? Now, accessing the device via its IP address in the browser only works when viewing the standard site, but trying to load the customized site results in a 404 error. The non-customized page that shows the BM screen works perfectly. Any help or troubleshooting would be appreciated.

Hello [user_name], A 404 error means the website doesn't exist, so something likely went wrong during the transfer process. I recommend removing the SD card from the [product_name] device, reformatting it on your computer, then reinserting it and trying to upload the [document] program again. Kind regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced a 'Download Failed! SD Card isn't ready' error when transferring a custom webpage that included images from the standard libraries to the SD card of a [product_name] version 8 device using [product_name] Web Editor. The issue appeared after adding images, while earlier uploads went smoothly, suggesting a potential problem with file handling or SD card readiness. The default webpage remains accessible, but the custom site returns a 404 error, indicating that deployment may have failed or was incomplete.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects dependable uploading of customized webpages, including those with images from the default libraries, to the [product_name] version 8 device's SD card without encountering errors. They anticipate reliable SD card functionality and successful deployment so that the customized webpage can be accessed through a browser.
